title: Stdlib - String - 1 [Operations]
description:
## String Operations
You've used `std::string` for text, but it has powerful built-in methods:

- `str.length()` or `str.size()` - character count
- `str.substr(start, len)` - extract a portion
- `str.find("text")` - find position of text (returns `std::string::npos` if not found)
- `str.append("text")` - add to the end (same as `str += "text"`)
- `str.replace(start, len, "new")` - replace a portion
- `str.erase(start, len)` - remove a portion
- `str[i]` - access character at index i

```cpp
std::string name = "CBitOS";
std::cout << name.length();        // 6
std::cout << name.substr(0, 4);    // CBit
std::cout << name.find("OS");      // 4
name.append(" v2");
std::cout << name;                 // CBitOS v2
```

## Assignment:
CBitOS stores the current version as a string. Given the version string:
1. Print its length
2. Extract and print just the version number (after `v`)
3. Find and print the position of the dash
4. Replace `beta` with `stable`
5. Print the final string
hint: Use find to locate the 'v', then substr from there. The dash is at index 6.
